```{r,echo=FALSE}
options(scipen=99)
r = sample(2:16,1)/100
n = sample(c(6,12,52,100,365),1)

y = (1+r/n)^n-1

ans = paste0(sprintf("%.3f",y*100),"%")

```

Question
========

An investment compounds with an interest rate of `r sprintf("%.3f",r*100)`% and a compound frequency of `r n` per year. What is the **effective annual yield**?

Express your answer as a percentage, rounded to the nearest thousandth of a percent. Include trailing zeros if necessary and include the % symbol. For example, if you calculate the effective annual yield is 0.1234025, write your answer as `12.340%`.

Solution
========

The [textbook](https://openstax.org/books/contemporary-mathematics/pages/6-4-compound-interest) provides this formula:

$$Y=\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^n-1$$

where $Y$ is the effective annual yield, $r$ is the (nominal) interest rate in decimal form, and $n$ is the number of compoundings per year. Plug in the numbers.

$$Y=\left(1+\frac{`r r`}{`r n`}\right)^{`r n`}-1$$

$$Y=`r y`$$

Thus, your answer should be ``r ans``
